To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

convex risk measures on sets of financial portfolios can be represented by probability contents if and only if they are law invariant, and by probability measures if and only if, in addition, they satisfy the criterion of Follmer and Shied.

• A convex risk measure on a set of financial positions can be represented as an expectation with respect to a probability measure if and only if it satisfies the following criterion: For every sequence of positions converging to the zero position, there is a sequence of positions such that the risk measure of each element is smaller than the risk measure of the limit position and the sequence of positions converges to the zero position.
convex risk measures on a Polish space can be represented by probability measures if and only if the sets of scenarios form a Polish space.
